text: Three launches. Three failures. And money for just one more try.
Twenty oh six. SpaceX's first rocket lifts off from a tiny island in the Pacific.
Thirty seconds later, it's on fire and falling into the reef.
Twenty oh seven. This time it reaches space. Then the second stage starts to spin, and never makes orbit.
August twenty oh eight. The third try. The stages collide after separation. Everything is lost.
Elon Musk later said he only had money for three attempts. And Tesla was running out of cash at the same time.
Less than two months later, one last rocket stands on the pad. If it fails, it's over.
Stage separation. Clean. The engine keeps burning.
The first privately built liquid-fueled rocket ever to reach orbit. Three months later, NASA signed a one point six billion dollar contract.
Every SpaceX rocket flying today started with that fourth try.
